column1: # obligations.tsv -- the DENOMINATOR for "this collector's link handling is proven".
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AND WHY IT IS NOT A LIST OF THE PROOFS.
# A list of proofs, or of what the test suite covers, describes the NUMERATOR: it
# can only ever say what exists, so read as coverage it answers "what did we
# prove" and never "what must we prove". An obligation nobody has approached is
# not representable in it. The rows below are authored from the code paths that
# can lose links -- the address rewriter, the expansion planner, the ledger's
# verdicts -- independently of what happens to be proven, so that an absent proof
# shows up as an open row rather than as nothing at all.
# A test does not discharge a row. A unit test covers the one input written in
# it; an obligation is a statement about every input. Several rows below are
# exercised by tests/link_shortener_test.pl and the pg tests, and all of them are
# still open.
# status: proven  -- discharged_by names lemmas that exist in a file that checks o.k.
#         partial -- proven on a FRAGMENT of the input domain only. Not a proven
#                    row: counting it as one is the over-claim this file prevents.
#         open    -- no proof.
# discharged_by is empty while nothing discharges the row.
# id
# EVERY ROW CITES TWO THINGS, AND NEEDS BOTH.
# The LPTP lemmas prove the law about the mirror under proofs/kernel/ —
# LPTP reads definite clauses and negation of ground goals, and the shipped
# modules are written with if_/3, memberd_t/3, tfilter/3 and zcompare/3, so
# they are restated there in the fragment it reads.
# tests/proofs_bridge_test.pl is what makes the law a statement about the
# collector rather than about a file nobody ships: it runs each mirror and
# its shipped counterpart over the same inputs and fails on any difference,
# allowing exactly two translations — a character as its code, a status as
# an atom. It runs with the suite, so a mirror that drifts is a red build
# and not a quiet lie.
# A row with nothing checked attached is deleted rather than parked: an
# obligation nobody discharges reads, after a month, as one somebody did.
# What is wanted and unproven belongs in proofs/README.md, in prose no tool
# can mistake for a guarantee.
A1
column4: permalink/2 is idempotent: reducing an address that is already a permalink changes nothing
column7: The ledger is keyed by address, so a permalink that moves on a second reduction would key one article under two rows and have it asked about twice. PARTIAL: proven for an address that carries no query at all, where the reduction is the identity and a second pass cannot move it. An address WITH a query needs split_params/2 and join_params/2 to be inverse on the parameters that survive the filter, and the filter to be idempotent on them; neither is proven.

column1: A2
column4: permalink/2 changes only the query part: scheme, host and path are preserved
column5: proofs/kernel/recogniser.pr: permalink:query:only, permalink:nosplit, rejoin:extends:base, split_at:functional + tests/proofs_bridge_test.pl
column7: It drops campaign parameters by splitting at the first ? and filtering; nothing stops a rejoin from losing the host, and a mangled host is a link a reader cannot open.

column1: A4
column4: rewrite_urls/3 is the identity when no pair's short form occurs in the text
column5: proofs/kernel/recogniser.pr: rewrite:identity, rewrite:identity:exact, rewrite:functional, first_match:functional + tests/proofs_bridge_test.pl
column7: Stronger than A3 and the one that matters for the day pass, which rewrites a whole day's rows from one pair list: a pair meant for another post must leave this one untouched.

column1: A5
column4: every address urls_in_text/2 yields is a contiguous subsequence of the text
column5: proofs/kernel/recogniser.pr: urls_in_text:contiguous, urls_in_text:contiguous:sim, take_while_not:append, piece_of:append, append:assoc, append:assoc2 + tests/proofs_bridge_test.pl
column7: It scans character by character and trims a punctuation suffix. An address assembled from pieces of the post, rather than cut out of it, is a link nobody wrote.

column1: A6
column4: shortened_urls_in_text/2 yields a subset of urls_in_text/2, and is duplicate-free
column5: proofs/kernel/recogniser.pr: shortened:subset:nodup, unique:subset, unique:nodup, unique:preserves:notin, filter_shortened:subset, without:notin, without:subset, without:preserves:notin, urls_in_text:functional + tests/proofs_bridge_test.pl
column7: Duplicate-freeness is what makes one token shared by many posts cost one question. A duplicate spends the budget twice on the same link.

column1: A7
column4: destination_url/2 prefers the noscript meta refresh over the canonical link
column7: The interstitials these redirectors answer with carry their own canonical link, which claims the interstitial. Reading it instead of the refresh target stores the redirector as the article.

column1: A8
column4: trim_trailing/2 removes only a suffix of its input, and only punctuation characters
column5: proofs/kernel/recogniser.pr: trim_trailing:punct_suffix, drop_trailing:punct_prefix, trim_trailing:functional, reverse:append, reverse:involution, all_punct:reverse, all_punct:append + tests/proofs_bridge_test.pl
column7: It reverses, drops, and reverses back. A reverse that is not undone, or a dropped character that was part of the path, silently shortens the address.

column1: A9
column4: shortened_url_t/2 answers at most one verdict about an address, and that verdict is true or false
column7: A condition that fails rather than answering false makes the whole scan fail, and the post is then stored with no expansion at all -- the repository's recorded failure class is a helper that fails instead of answering. The statement says what the lemmas prove and no more. That there is ALWAYS a verdict -- totality -- is not proven and is not claimed here: totality needs every membership and prefix test to answer rather than fail, which rests on equality of two characters being decided, and that needs groundness (gr) reasoning these proofs do not set up.

column4: each reified condition is functional (one truth value per input) and boolean (that value is true or false)
column5: proofs/kernel/recogniser.pr: cond:boolean, cond:functional, memb:boolean, memb:functional, prefix:boolean, prefix:functional, contains_sub:boolean, contains_sub:functional, found_truth:boolean, found_truth:functional, url_start:boolean, url_start:functional, dif:boolean, dif:functional, branded_redirector:boolean, branded_redirector:functional, generic_host:boolean, generic_host:functional, opaque_short_path:boolean, opaque_short_path:functional, segment_truth:boolean, segment_truth:functional, all_token_chars:boolean, all_token_chars:functional, any:boolean, any:functional, opaque_shape:boolean, opaque_shape:functional, short_enough:boolean, short_enough:functional, at_least:boolean, at_least:functional, at_most:boolean, at_most:functional, len_in:boolean, len_in:functional, shortened_url:boolean, shortened_url:functional, functional_param:boolean, functional_param:functional, tracking_param:boolean, tracking_param:functional, any_prefix:boolean, any_prefix:functional, negate:boolean, negate:functional + tests/proofs_bridge_test.pl
column7: if_/3 is sound only on conditions that are both. A condition with two solutions turns one post into several answers on backtracking; one with a third value makes if_/3 fail where the code reads as a total dispatch. Every condition of the module is covered: the thirteen character sets through cond:boolean and cond:functional, the rest one lemma pair each. code_in_t/4 and range_truth/3 appear as the table tests and as at_least/at_most; code_t/3 as the five one-character tags.

column1: P1
column4: the expansion planner never asks more questions than its budget allows
column7: The law the loss is about: eight hundred unseen links were asked about back to back. planner:decision:cost is the accounting for one address -- a decision either costs nothing and returns the allowance untouched, or is a question and returns it one smaller, with no third case and no case where it grows; planner:budget threads that through a whole day's links by induction, so there is no path on which the thread is dropped. Proven of the mirror, which owes P4.

column1: P2
column4: every substitution the planner makes comes from what the ledger already knows
column5: proofs/kernel/planner.pr: planner:substitutions:known, planner:decisions:substitute:known, planner:plan:substitution:decision, planner:known_answer:member + tests/proofs_bridge_test.pl
column7: A pair whose expansion came from somewhere else -- a stale variable, a neighbouring link's answer -- stores one article's address under another's post, and the rewrite is irreversible once the day is ranked. The chain is proven end to end: a substitution names the address it was decided for, that address had an expanded answer in Known, and sorting the decisions into the plan invents no pair. Proven of the mirror, which owes P4.

column1: P3
column4: a link the ledger calls blocked, pending or dead is never substituted
column5: proofs/kernel/planner.pr: planner:answered:never:substituted, planner:answered:left, planner:blocked:leave, planner:pending:leave, planner:dead:leave + tests/proofs_bridge_test.pl
column7: Blocked and pending mean nobody has an address yet; dead means there is none to have. Substituting one writes a redirector token, or an empty address, over a link that still works for a reader. Each of the three is proven on its own answer, which is how the dispatch reads it. Proven of the mirror, which owes P4.

column1: L1
column3: refusal_status/2, outcome_of/4, destination_outcome/3, answer_of_outcome/2 -- all in src/link_expansion.pl since the planner was extracted
column4: only 404 and 410 map to dead; a 200 with no destination in the page never yields resolved
column5: proofs/kernel/planner.pr: verdict:dead:only:404:410, verdict:answer:dead:only:404:410, verdict:404:dead, verdict:410:dead, verdict:other:blocked, verdict:200:through:destination, verdict:no_destination:never:resolved, verdict:resolved:differs + tests/proofs_bridge_test.pl
column7: dead is final: the link is never asked about again. A 403 block page read as dead is how 812 live links were written off. Both directions are proven, so the law is not satisfied by a relation that calls nothing dead: 404 and 410 ARE dead, every other code is blocked, and no other code reaches dead through answer_of_outcome/2. For the second half, the 200 branch is proven to read the reply through the recogniser and nothing else, and a finding of none is proven to yield unavailable; whether a page with no destination IS found to claim none is the recogniser's obligation, not this one.

column1: P4
column4: each mirror relation answers what the shipped predicate answers
column7: Every row above is proven of a mirror, not of src/. A proof about a mirror says nothing about this collector unless the mirror answers what the module answers, so P1, P2, P3 and L1 each name this row as the one they rest on. PARTIAL: the bridge compares the two on what production carries -- 241 addresses, 4 posts, 4 pages, 3 substitutions, 6 status codes, 6 outcomes and 5 planner scenarios, budget included -- which is a corpus and not a proof. Equality of the relations for every input is not established and would need the mirror and the shipped clauses related mechanically rather than compared on examples.
